<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**12** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5802d424cf452e4e20ff3e902984a6d6fe84196a` — the merge of head `425681c5f122263a0e8f4e1ca6eb8bc9dc264e4e` into base `ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5802d424cf452e4e20ff3e902984a6d6fe84196a && git checkout 5802d424cf452e4e20ff3e902984a6d6fe84196a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd 425681c5f122263a0e8f4e1ca6eb8bc9dc264e4e && git checkout -B drift-repro ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd && git merge --no-ff 425681c5f122263a0e8f4e1ca6eb8bc9dc264e4e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `64c1008cc782fc263edfa9c49bbb172d35fa39b2`
Local-runs: none

This is the lane seat's own review of record. It is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone (face `declaration`). No path of the diff is a published schema or a governed path: `packages/spec/**` and the server are untouched. `check-governed-merges --pr 31835` reads NOT governed (0 of 40 paths, 1265 lines).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@object-ui/i18n` is published and only widens.** `recycleBin.page.*` is added to all 11 packs, with two count families, `related` and `emptied`, whose plural rows follow each language's categories. No key is removed or reworded.
- **`@objectstack/platform-objects` gains one Setup nav entry**: `nav_recycle_bin`, `type: 'component'`, `componentRef: 'data:recycle-bin'`, in `group_configuration`. Its label is in all 11 bundles, and the source digests are in the 10 hash files.
  - It has no `requiredPermissions`. The grant is per object, so no single permission names it. A caller who manages no bin sees the page say so, and no bin read is sent.
  - The entry is data inside an existing contribution list. It is not an authorable key, value or meaning.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` is private.** `CatalogAssignmentPage` gains an optional `select`, and `renderSection` gains a second argument. Both existing callers pass a one-argument function, which still type-checks.
- **The gates match the doors, read against `origin/main`.**
  - The page lists an object when `objectPermissionGrants(perm, 'manageRecycleBin')` holds. That is the spec fold `packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/list.ts` asks, so the console lists only bins the door would answer.
  - Restore is offered on `allowRestoreOwnDeleted`, which `manageRecycleBin` implies (`permission.zod.ts:294-296`), so every listed entry can be restored.
  - The doors' shapes are `packages/client` `recycleBin.list` (`{ entries, hasMore }`) and `recycleBin.empty` (`{ removed }`).
  - The door masks the snapshot to the fields the caller may read, and the page names a row from those fields only.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is RIGHT.** No author-written key, value or meaning changes.
- **Accept sets:** none change.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/30239-recycle-bin-setup-page.md` marks `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` as `patch`.
- Both declaration lines are at line start, in the changeset and in the PR body.
- That is RIGHT: a widening ships as `patch`. PR 1's nit N1 is closed, because this changeset names `RecordDeleteToastAction`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Nit N4:** Restore and Load more do not disable each other.
  - If a restore finishes while a Load more read is in flight, the server's offsets shift by one, and the next page can skip one entry at the boundary. The entry is not lost: a re-pick or Retry shows it.
  - Accepted. A later touch can disable Restore while `loadingMore` is set.
- **Accepted deviation:** a formula `nameField` reads its fallback in the list, because the snapshot holds stored columns only. This is named in the PR's Acceptance notes.
- `open_questions`: none.
